questions.prompt: Which statement is an example of self-awareness?
options: I know I work well when I make a plan.
Everyone should always agree with me.
I never need help from anyone.
Rules only apply when a teacher is watching.
questions.correctAnswer: I know I work well when I make a plan.
questions.explanation: Self-awareness means understanding your thoughts, strengths, habits, and areas for growth.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize personal strengths and values that guide responsible choices.

questions.prompt: A learner who can name two things they do well is showing which life skill?
options: Recognition of personal strengths
Avoidance of responsibility
Peer pressure
Poor communication
questions.correctAnswer: Recognition of personal strengths
questions.explanation: Knowing your strengths helps you build confidence and use your abilities responsibly.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify personal abilities and use them positively in school and community life.

questions.prompt: What is a personal value?
options: A belief that guides choices and behavior
A school subject chosen by a teacher
A game played during break time
A mark written on a report card
questions.correctAnswer: A belief that guides choices and behavior
questions.explanation: Values such as honesty and respect influence how a person makes decisions.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how personal values influence daily choices.

questions.prompt: Why is it helpful for a learner to know their weaknesses?
options: It helps the learner choose areas to improve.
It proves the learner cannot succeed.
It gives the learner a reason to stop trying.
It allows the learner to blame classmates.
questions.correctAnswer: It helps the learner choose areas to improve.
questions.explanation: Understanding weaknesses is useful when it leads to planning, practice, and seeking support.
questions.learningOutcome: Use self-reflection to identify areas for personal improvement.

questions.prompt: Which action is most likely to build healthy self-esteem?
options: Learning from mistakes and trying again
Laughing at classmates who struggle
Pretending to know everything
Avoiding all difficult activities
questions.correctAnswer: Learning from mistakes and trying again
questions.explanation: Healthy self-esteem grows when learners accept mistakes as chances to improve.
questions.learningOutcome: Demonstrate behaviors that strengthen positive self-esteem.

questions.prompt: During group work, Amina notices that she often interrupts others. Which skill is she using when she recognizes this habit?
options: Self-awareness
Peer pressure
First aid
Saving
questions.correctAnswer: Self-awareness
questions.explanation: Recognizing one's own behavior is part of self-awareness and can lead to better teamwork.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize personal habits that affect interaction with others.

questions.prompt: Which goal is realistic for a Grade 7 learner who wants to improve reading?
options: Read one storybook chapter each weekday for two weeks.
Read every book in the library by tomorrow.
Stop doing all other subjects until reading improves.
Wait for reading to improve without practice.
questions.correctAnswer: Read one storybook chapter each weekday for two weeks.
questions.explanation: A realistic goal has a clear action and a time frame that the learner can manage.
questions.learningOutcome: Set realistic goals for learning and personal growth.

questions.prompt: How can a learner show confidence without boasting?
options: Share ideas respectfully and listen to others.
Speak loudly so nobody else can contribute.
Claim to be better than every classmate.
Ignore feedback from teachers.
questions.correctAnswer: Share ideas respectfully and listen to others.
questions.explanation: Confidence is healthy when it is combined with respect for other people.
questions.learningOutcome: Express confidence respectfully in school situations.

questions.prompt: Which record would best help a learner reflect on progress over a month?
options: A journal of goals, actions, challenges, and lessons
A list of classmates' mistakes
A timetable with no review notes
A page of copied slogans
questions.correctAnswer: A journal of goals, actions, challenges, and lessons
questions.explanation: A reflection journal helps a learner connect actions with growth and future improvement.
questions.learningOutcome: Use reflection tools to monitor personal progress and learning habits.

questions.prompt: Which plan best supports a learner who wants to strengthen positive identity during the term?
options: Identify strengths, choose values, set goals, seek support, and review progress.
Copy a popular learner's behavior without thinking about personal values.
Avoid all activities where mistakes might happen.
Wait until the end of the term to think about growth.
questions.correctAnswer: Identify strengths, choose values, set goals, seek support, and review progress.
questions.explanation: Positive identity is strengthened by knowing oneself, acting on values, and reviewing growth over time.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a personal growth plan that reflects strengths, values, and support systems.

questions.prompt: What is a helpful first step when you feel very angry?
options: Pause and take a few deep breaths.
Shout immediately at the nearest person.
Break something to show the anger.
Post an angry message online.
questions.correctAnswer: Pause and take a few deep breaths.
questions.explanation: Pausing gives the mind time to calm down before choosing a response.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify safe first steps for managing strong emotions.

questions.prompt: Which is a healthy way to cope with sadness?
options: Talk to a trusted adult or supportive friend.
Stay silent forever and avoid everyone.
Blame another learner for every feeling.
Use insults to hide the sadness.
questions.correctAnswer: Talk to a trusted adult or supportive friend.
questions.explanation: Talking to a trusted person can provide comfort, guidance, and practical support.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose healthy strategies for coping with sadness and disappointment.

questions.prompt: When can stress become harmful?
options: When it continues for long and disrupts normal activities
Only when a learner has no homework
Whenever a learner tries something new
Only during games and sports
questions.correctAnswer: When it continues for long and disrupts normal activities
questions.explanation: Long-lasting stress can affect sleep, learning, relationships, and health.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe signs that stress may require support.

questions.prompt: Which sign may show that a learner is experiencing exam stress?
options: Difficulty sleeping because of worry
Enjoying a balanced meal
Asking questions during revision
Arriving early for class
questions.correctAnswer: Difficulty sleeping because of worry
questions.explanation: Worry that interferes with sleep can be a sign of stress that needs healthy management.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize common signs of stress among learners.

questions.prompt: A classmate seems stressed after failing a test. Which response shows empathy?
options: Listen kindly and encourage the classmate to seek help.
Laugh and tell others about the mark.
Ignore the classmate until they stop worrying.
Tell the classmate that only high marks matter.
questions.correctAnswer: Listen kindly and encourage the classmate to seek help.
questions.explanation: Empathy involves understanding another person's feelings and offering respectful support.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply empathy when supporting peers who face disappointment.

questions.prompt: Which statement is assertive when classmates suggest an unsafe activity?
options: I do not want to join that; let us choose another activity.
You are all terrible people.
I will join because I cannot say no.
I will stay quiet and hope someone notices.
questions.correctAnswer: I do not want to join that; let us choose another activity.
questions.explanation: Assertive communication is clear and respectful while protecting personal safety and values.
questions.learningOutcome: Use assertive language to resist unsafe choices.

questions.prompt: What is emotional self-control?
options: Managing feelings before acting
Refusing to feel any emotion
Controlling other people's choices
Hiding every problem from trusted adults
questions.correctAnswer: Managing feelings before acting
questions.explanation: Self-control helps a person respond thoughtfully instead of reacting in a harmful way.
questions.learningOutcome: Define emotional self-control and its purpose.

questions.prompt: A learner loses a game and congratulates the winners. Which quality is being shown?
options: Resilience
Jealousy
Dishonesty
Carelessness
questions.correctAnswer: Resilience
questions.explanation: Resilience includes handling disappointment positively and continuing to learn from experience.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize resilient behavior after setbacks.

questions.prompt: Before a class presentation, Brian feels afraid. Which plan is most helpful?
options: Practise, breathe slowly, and ask for guidance.
Pretend to be sick every time he presents.
Insult classmates so they will not listen.
Throw away his notes and refuse to speak.
questions.correctAnswer: Practise, breathe slowly, and ask for guidance.
questions.explanation: Preparation, calm breathing, and support can reduce fear and improve confidence.
questions.learningOutcome: Plan healthy strategies for managing fear in school activities.

questions.prompt: Why should learners avoid insulting themselves after making mistakes?
options: Negative self-talk can reduce confidence and effort.
Mistakes should always be hidden from teachers.
Only perfect learners deserve encouragement.
Self-insults make revision easier.
questions.correctAnswer: Negative self-talk can reduce confidence and effort.
questions.explanation: Kind and honest self-talk supports learning because mistakes can show what needs practice.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze how self-talk affects confidence and learning.

questions.prompt: What does active listening mean?
options: Paying attention and checking that you understood
Planning your reply while the other person speaks
Interrupting to finish another person's sentence
Looking away until the speaker stops
questions.correctAnswer: Paying attention and checking that you understood
questions.explanation: Active listening shows respect and helps avoid misunderstanding.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe active listening as a communication skill.

questions.prompt: Which body language usually shows respectful listening?
options: Facing the speaker and maintaining polite eye contact
Turning away and laughing with a friend
Rolling eyes while the speaker talks
Walking out without explanation
questions.correctAnswer: Facing the speaker and maintaining polite eye contact
questions.explanation: Respectful body language helps the speaker feel heard and valued.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify non-verbal behaviors that support respectful communication.

questions.prompt: If you do not understand class instructions, which question is most respectful?
options: Please explain the first step again.
Why are you making this so hard?
Can someone else do my work?
Why should I listen?
questions.correctAnswer: Please explain the first step again.
questions.explanation: A respectful clarification question is specific and helps the learner continue with the task.
questions.learningOutcome: Ask respectful questions to clarify instructions.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is an example of an I-statement in a disagreement?
options: I feel ignored when I am not given a turn to speak.
You always ruin everything.
Everyone knows you are the problem.
Nobody should listen to you.
questions.correctAnswer: I feel ignored when I am not given a turn to speak.
questions.explanation: An I-statement explains feelings and needs without attacking the other person.
questions.learningOutcome: Use I-statements to communicate feelings during conflict.

questions.prompt: Which pair of actions is part of effective communication?
options: Speaking clearly and listening carefully
Shouting loudly and blaming others
Guessing meaning and refusing questions
Ignoring feedback and changing the topic
questions.correctAnswer: Speaking clearly and listening carefully
questions.explanation: Communication works best when both speaking and listening are done respectfully.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify key behaviors in effective communication.

questions.prompt: Why should learners avoid spreading rumours?
options: Rumours can harm relationships and reputations.
Rumours always make people more responsible.
Rumours are the fastest way to solve conflict.
Rumours replace the need for facts.
questions.correctAnswer: Rumours can harm relationships and reputations.
questions.explanation: Rumours can be unfair, untrue, and damaging to trust among learners.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why truthful communication is important in relationships.

questions.prompt: A group leader summarizes each member's idea before the group votes. Which skill is the leader using?
options: Inclusive communication
Peer pressure
Avoidance
Careless listening
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusive communication
questions.explanation: Inclusive communication gives group members a chance to be heard before decisions are made.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze communication practices that support fair participation in groups.

questions.prompt: Which online message shows respectful disagreement?
options: I disagree with your point because the evidence suggests another view.
Only foolish people think like you.
I will embarrass you in the class chat.
Nobody should ever read your posts.
questions.correctAnswer: I disagree with your point because the evidence suggests another view.
questions.explanation: Respectful disagreement focuses on ideas and evidence instead of insulting a person.
questions.learningOutcome: Communicate respectfully when using digital platforms.

questions.prompt: What should you do if a joke you made hurts another learner?
options: Apologize and stop using the joke.
Repeat the joke more loudly.
Tell the learner they are too sensitive.
Ask others to laugh at the learner.
questions.correctAnswer: Apologize and stop using the joke.
questions.explanation: A sincere apology and changed behavior show respect for the other person's feelings.
questions.learningOutcome: Respond respectfully when words or actions hurt others.

questions.prompt: Which comment gives useful feedback on a class poster?
options: Your poster is clear; add labels to the diagram.
This is bad and I do not like it.
Mine is better than yours.
You should stop trying posters.
questions.correctAnswer: Your poster is clear; add labels to the diagram.
questions.explanation: Useful feedback names a strength and suggests a clear improvement.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate feedback that supports improvement and respect.

questions.prompt: A healthy friendship is built on which qualities?
options: Trust, respect, and support
Fear, secrecy, and pressure
Boasting, insults, and jealousy
Threats, rumours, and revenge
questions.correctAnswer: Trust, respect, and support
questions.explanation: Healthy friendships make people feel valued, safe, and supported.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify qualities of healthy friendships.

questions.prompt: What is peer pressure?
options: Influence from age-mates to act in a certain way
A timetable made by the class teacher
A school rule about reporting time
A method of cleaning the classroom
questions.correctAnswer: Influence from age-mates to act in a certain way
questions.explanation: Peer pressure can influence choices positively or negatively.
questions.learningOutcome: Define peer pressure and recognize its influence.

questions.prompt: A classmate pressures you to skip cleaning duty. What is a responsible response?
options: Refuse politely and complete the duty.
Run away and leave the work for others.
Hide the cleaning tools from the class.
Insult the classmate in front of everyone.
questions.correctAnswer: Refuse politely and complete the duty.
questions.explanation: Responsible learners keep commitments and can refuse negative pressure respectfully.
questions.learningOutcome: Respond responsibly to peer pressure in school routines.

questions.prompt: How is bullying different from an ordinary disagreement?
options: Bullying involves repeated harmful behavior or a power imbalance.
Bullying always helps people become close friends.
Bullying is only a private joke between friends.
Bullying happens only when learners disagree about homework.
questions.correctAnswer: Bullying involves repeated harmful behavior or a power imbalance.
questions.explanation: Bullying is serious because it targets a person through repeated harm, fear, or misuse of power.
questions.learningOutcome: Distinguish bullying from ordinary disagreement or conflict.

questions.prompt: What should a safe bystander do after seeing bullying at school?
options: Report to a trusted adult and support the learner safely.
Record the bullying and share it for fun.
Join the bullying to avoid being targeted.
Ignore it because it is not their problem.
questions.correctAnswer: Report to a trusted adult and support the learner safely.
questions.explanation: A safe bystander seeks help and supports the targeted learner without increasing danger.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose safe bystander actions when bullying occurs.

questions.prompt: What does empathy mean?
options: Trying to understand another person's feelings
Forcing others to agree with your opinion
Winning every argument in class
Avoiding people who need support
questions.correctAnswer: Trying to understand another person's feelings
questions.explanation: Empathy helps people respond with kindness and respect.
questions.learningOutcome: Define empathy as a relationship skill.

questions.prompt: When team members disagree about a class activity, what should they do first?
options: Let each person explain calmly.
Cancel the activity immediately.
Choose the loudest person's idea.
Stop talking to one another.
questions.correctAnswer: Let each person explain calmly.
questions.explanation: Listening calmly helps the team understand the problem before choosing a solution.
questions.learningOutcome: Use listening as a first step in peaceful conflict resolution.

questions.prompt: Which action shows respect for diversity in class?
options: Learning how classmates' backgrounds shape their views
Mocking a classmate's language or customs
Refusing to work with anyone who is different
Assuming one group is better than all others
questions.correctAnswer: Learning how classmates' backgrounds shape their views
questions.explanation: Respect for diversity means valuing differences and treating people fairly.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze ways of showing respect for different backgrounds and experiences.

questions.prompt: A rumour causes an argument between two learners. Which response best helps resolve the conflict?
options: Check facts and talk calmly with those involved.
Spread the rumour to more learners.
Refuse to listen to either learner.
Punish both learners without hearing them.
questions.correctAnswer: Check facts and talk calmly with those involved.
questions.explanation: Conflict resolution should be based on facts, respectful listening, and fair discussion.
questions.learningOutcome: Design a fair response to conflict caused by misinformation.

questions.prompt: Why is it important to set boundaries in friendships?
options: Boundaries protect personal safety, time, and values.
Boundaries stop all friendships from growing.
Boundaries prove that friends cannot be trusted.
Boundaries mean a learner should never help anyone.
questions.correctAnswer: Boundaries protect personal safety, time, and values.
questions.explanation: Healthy boundaries help people relate with respect and avoid harmful pressure.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze the role of boundaries in healthy friendships.

questions.prompt: What does assertiveness mean?
options: Standing up for yourself respectfully
Getting your way by threatening others
Keeping silent about every problem
Doing whatever friends demand
questions.correctAnswer: Standing up for yourself respectfully
questions.explanation: Assertiveness combines clear expression with respect for others.
questions.learningOutcome: Define assertiveness as a respectful communication skill.

questions.prompt: A friend asks you to share private information about another learner. What should you say?
options: I cannot share that; it is private.
I will tell you if you promise to laugh.
Let us post it in the class group.
I will trade it for another secret.
questions.correctAnswer: I cannot share that; it is private.
questions.explanation: Respecting privacy protects trust and avoids harm.
questions.learningOutcome: Use respectful words to protect privacy and boundaries.

questions.prompt: Which situation is an example of negative peer pressure?
options: Friends dare you to break a school rule.
Friends invite you to join a study group.
Friends remind you to return a library book.
Friends help you practise for a presentation.
questions.correctAnswer: Friends dare you to break a school rule.
questions.explanation: Negative peer pressure pushes someone toward harmful or irresponsible choices.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify negative peer pressure in familiar situations.

questions.prompt: What can help a learner resist peer pressure before it happens?
options: Practising a firm refusal in advance
Waiting until friends make every choice
Promising to follow any group decision
Avoiding all adults who give guidance
questions.correctAnswer: Practising a firm refusal in advance
questions.explanation: Practising refusal makes it easier to respond confidently under pressure.
questions.learningOutcome: Prepare refusal skills for handling negative peer pressure.

questions.prompt: Why is it helpful to choose friends with positive values?
options: They can encourage responsible choices.
They will make every decision for you.
They will never disagree with you.
They remove the need for family guidance.
questions.correctAnswer: They can encourage responsible choices.
questions.explanation: Friends influence behavior, so positive values can support good choices and growth.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how positive friendships influence personal choices.

questions.prompt: What should a learner do after receiving repeated insulting messages online?
options: Save evidence, block the sender, and report to a trusted adult.
Reply with worse insults.
Forward the messages to embarrass the sender.
Meet the sender alone to argue.
questions.correctAnswer: Save evidence, block the sender, and report to a trusted adult.
questions.explanation: Cyberbullying should be handled by protecting safety, keeping evidence, and seeking help.
questions.learningOutcome: Respond safely to cyberbullying and harmful online messages.

questions.prompt: Which is a safe personal boundary with classmates?
options: Refusing touch or teasing that makes you uncomfortable
Allowing friends to control all your choices
Sharing passwords to prove friendship
Keeping quiet when someone threatens you
questions.correctAnswer: Refusing touch or teasing that makes you uncomfortable
questions.explanation: A boundary helps protect personal dignity, safety, and comfort.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify safe boundaries in peer relationships.

questions.prompt: Which action can help repair trust after hurting a friend?
options: Admit the mistake, apologize, and change behavior.
Pretend nothing happened.
Blame the friend for feeling hurt.
Tell other learners to take sides.
questions.correctAnswer: Admit the mistake, apologize, and change behavior.
questions.explanation: Trust is rebuilt through honesty, responsibility, and consistent respectful behavior.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply responsible steps for repairing damaged relationships.

questions.prompt: In a group task, one learner is being excluded. Which action best promotes inclusion?
options: Invite the learner to take a meaningful role in the task.
Give the learner no work so the group finishes faster.
Make jokes about the learner's ability.
Report that the learner refused to help without asking.
questions.correctAnswer: Invite the learner to take a meaningful role in the task.
questions.explanation: Inclusion means giving people fair chances to participate and contribute.
questions.learningOutcome: Create inclusive responses that support participation in group activities.

questions.prompt: A learner is offered alcohol at a party. Which response is safest?
options: Say no, leave the situation, and tell a trusted adult.
Take it to avoid being laughed at.
Taste it only once to please friends.
Hide it in a bag and keep quiet.
questions.correctAnswer: Say no, leave the situation, and tell a trusted adult.
questions.explanation: Refusing harmful substances and seeking support protects health and safety.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze safe responses to pressure involving harmful substances.

questions.prompt: What is the first step in responsible decision making?
options: Identify the choice or problem clearly.
Choose quickly without thinking.
Ask friends to decide everything.
Ignore possible consequences.
questions.correctAnswer: Identify the choice or problem clearly.
questions.explanation: A clear understanding of the decision helps a learner compare options wisely.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify the first step in making responsible decisions.

questions.prompt: Why should a learner think about consequences before acting?
options: To understand how choices may affect self and others
To make decisions slower for no reason
To avoid asking for guidance forever
To prove that every option is the same
questions.correctAnswer: To understand how choices may affect self and others
questions.explanation: Thinking about consequences helps learners avoid harm and choose responsibly.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why consequences matter in decision making.

questions.prompt: After listing possible solutions to a problem, what should a learner do next?
options: Compare the likely results of each option.
Pick the option that sounds easiest without thinking.
Stop because listing options is enough.
Choose the option that will annoy others.
questions.correctAnswer: Compare the likely results of each option.
questions.explanation: Comparing results helps a learner choose a solution that is practical and responsible.
questions.learningOutcome: Use comparison of options in problem solving.

questions.prompt: You find a phone on the school compound. Which choice shows responsibility?
options: Give it to a teacher or office for the owner.
Keep it until someone notices.
Sell it to another learner.
Remove the SIM card and hide it.
questions.correctAnswer: Give it to a teacher or office for the owner.
questions.explanation: Returning lost property through the proper office shows honesty and responsibility.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply honesty when handling lost property.

questions.prompt: Which choice protects personal health?
options: Washing hands before eating
Sharing a towel with many people
Eating food dropped on the ground
Ignoring a dirty wound
questions.correctAnswer: Washing hands before eating
questions.explanation: Handwashing helps prevent germs from entering the body through food.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify hygiene practices that protect health.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to use a phone all night before a test. Which decision is most responsible?
options: Switch it off and get enough sleep.
Stay awake to answer every message.
Hide the phone under the pillow and keep scrolling.
Skip the test because of tiredness.
questions.correctAnswer: Switch it off and get enough sleep.
questions.explanation: Enough sleep supports concentration, health, and responsible learning.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze choices that protect learning and wellbeing.

questions.prompt: How do values guide decisions?
options: They help decide what is acceptable and responsible.
They remove the need to think about consequences.
They make every learner choose the same hobby.
They only matter during assemblies.
questions.correctAnswer: They help decide what is acceptable and responsible.
questions.explanation: Values act like standards that guide choices in different situations.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the role of values in responsible decision making.

questions.prompt: Which question helps a learner judge whether an option is safe?
options: Could this harm me or someone else?
Will this make me look popular for one minute?
Can I hide this from every adult?
Will this make another learner afraid?
questions.correctAnswer: Could this harm me or someone else?
questions.explanation: Safety checks consider possible harm before a decision is made.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze risk by asking safety-focused questions before acting.

questions.prompt: A learner copies homework because they fear failing. Which solution addresses the problem responsibly?
options: Ask for help and plan time to finish the work honestly.
Copy faster so nobody notices.
Blame the subject for being difficult.
Convince others to copy too.
questions.correctAnswer: Ask for help and plan time to finish the work honestly.
questions.explanation: The responsible solution deals with the learning difficulty while maintaining honesty.
questions.learningOutcome: Create responsible solutions to academic pressure without dishonesty.

questions.prompt: When should a learner seek adult help for a problem?
options: When safety, harm, or serious conflict is involved
Only when the learner wants to avoid responsibility
Never, because all problems must be solved alone
Only after telling every classmate first
questions.correctAnswer: When safety, harm, or serious conflict is involved
questions.explanation: Trusted adults can help protect safety and guide serious problems.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify situations that require support from trusted adults.

questions.prompt: Which detail belongs in a SMART goal?
options: A specific action and time frame
A vague wish with no plan
A secret that nobody can review
A task chosen only to impress friends
questions.correctAnswer: A specific action and time frame
questions.explanation: A SMART goal is clearer when it names what will be done and by when.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify features of clear and realistic goals.

questions.prompt: Which goal is measurable?
options: Complete ten mathematics revision questions by Friday.
Become better at school one day.
Try hard whenever possible.
Read more if there is time.
questions.correctAnswer: Complete ten mathematics revision questions by Friday.
questions.explanation: A measurable goal includes a clear amount or evidence of completion.
questions.learningOutcome: Distinguish measurable goals from vague wishes.

questions.prompt: Why should a learner break a big goal into smaller steps?
options: Smaller steps make progress easier to track.
Smaller steps remove the need for effort.
Big goals should never be attempted.
Steps are useful only for sports.
questions.correctAnswer: Smaller steps make progress easier to track.
questions.explanation: Steps help a learner know what to do next and monitor progress.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why goals should be divided into manageable steps.

questions.prompt: Which tool can help with time management?
options: A weekly study and chores timetable
A blank notebook hidden in a bag
A list of excuses for late work
A poster with no tasks or times
questions.correctAnswer: A weekly study and chores timetable
questions.explanation: A timetable helps a learner plan duties, study, rest, and other activities.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify tools used to manage time responsibly.

questions.prompt: What does prioritizing tasks mean?
options: Doing important and urgent tasks first
Doing only the easiest tasks every day
Ignoring tasks that require effort
Waiting for someone else to choose
questions.correctAnswer: Doing important and urgent tasks first
questions.explanation: Prioritizing helps a learner use time well and meet responsibilities.
questions.learningOutcome: Define prioritizing as a time management skill.

questions.prompt: A group project is due next week. What should the group do first?
options: Agree on tasks, deadlines, and roles.
Wait until the night before the deadline.
Let one learner do everything alone.
Argue about marks before reading the task.
questions.correctAnswer: Agree on tasks, deadlines, and roles.
questions.explanation: Planning roles and deadlines early helps the group work fairly and finish on time.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze project needs and organize roles for timely completion.

questions.prompt: Which behavior shows responsibility for learning?
options: Preparing books and asking questions when stuck
Blaming the teacher before trying
Leaving assignments at home on purpose
Waiting for friends to copy notes
questions.correctAnswer: Preparing books and asking questions when stuck
questions.explanation: Responsible learners prepare, participate, and seek help when they need it.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain behaviors that show responsibility for learning.

questions.prompt: Which plan best balances school work and rest?
options: Plan study time, chores, play, meals, and sleep.
Study all night and skip sleep.
Play first and do assignments only if time remains.
Do chores during every lesson.
questions.correctAnswer: Plan study time, chores, play, meals, and sleep.
questions.explanation: Balance supports learning, health, family responsibility, and wellbeing.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze daily routines that balance responsibilities and wellbeing.

questions.prompt: Which example is a distraction during homework?
options: Constant social media notifications
A clear desk with needed books
A short planned break after work
A quiet study corner
questions.correctAnswer: Constant social media notifications
questions.explanation: Frequent notifications can interrupt concentration and slow learning.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify distractions that affect study time.

questions.prompt: A learner misses a weekly target twice. What is the most useful next step?
options: Review the plan, identify obstacles, and adjust the next steps.
Stop setting goals for the rest of the year.
Blame classmates for the missed target.
Pretend the target was never important.
questions.correctAnswer: Review the plan, identify obstacles, and adjust the next steps.
questions.explanation: Reviewing and adjusting a plan helps a learner keep improving after setbacks.
questions.learningOutcome: Create improved goal plans after reviewing progress and obstacles.

questions.prompt: At a pedestrian crossing in Kenya, what should a learner do before crossing?
options: Look right, left, and right again before crossing.
Run across without looking if friends are waiting.
Cross while reading a phone message.
Stand in the middle of the road to check traffic.
questions.correctAnswer: Look right, left, and right again before crossing.
questions.explanation: Checking both directions helps a pedestrian notice vehicles before entering the road.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safe pedestrian practices on Kenyan roads.

questions.prompt: Which action supports safety while travelling in a matatu?
options: Use a seat belt if available and keep your body inside the vehicle.
Lean out of the window to greet friends.
Distract the driver with shouting.
Jump out before the vehicle stops.
questions.correctAnswer: Use a seat belt if available and keep your body inside the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Safe passenger behavior reduces the risk of injury during travel.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose safe passenger behavior in public transport.

questions.prompt: What should learners do when a fire drill alarm rings?
options: Leave calmly using the agreed route.
Run back for bags and books.
Hide in the classroom.
Push others to reach the gate first.
questions.correctAnswer: Leave calmly using the agreed route.
questions.explanation: A calm evacuation using the planned route helps keep everyone safer.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify safe actions during school emergency drills.

questions.prompt: Which first aid action is suitable for a small cleanable cut?
options: Wash with clean water and cover with a clean dressing.
Rub soil into the cut to stop bleeding.
Ignore it until it becomes painful.
Share another learner's used bandage.
questions.correctAnswer: Wash with clean water and cover with a clean dressing.
questions.explanation: Cleaning and covering a small cut helps reduce infection risk while further help can be sought if needed.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply basic first aid steps for minor cuts.

questions.prompt: What is a safe response to a nosebleed at school?
options: Sit upright, lean slightly forward, and pinch the soft part of the nose.
Lie flat and tilt the head far backward.
Run around until the bleeding stops.
Put dirty paper deep inside the nose.
questions.correctAnswer: Sit upright, lean slightly forward, and pinch the soft part of the nose.
questions.explanation: Leaning slightly forward and pinching the soft nose area helps manage a nosebleed safely.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose safe first aid responses for common minor injuries.

questions.prompt: A stranger offers a learner a lift home. What is the safest response?
options: Refuse and move to a trusted adult or safe place.
Enter the vehicle to avoid sounding rude.
Give the stranger the home address.
Go along if the stranger smiles.
questions.correctAnswer: Refuse and move to a trusted adult or safe place.
questions.explanation: Personal safety comes first when an unknown person offers transport or asks for private details.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose safe responses to risky interactions with unknown people.

questions.prompt: Why should learners know emergency contacts?
options: To get help quickly during danger or illness
To call friends during lessons
To avoid reporting emergencies
To replace safety rules
questions.correctAnswer: To get help quickly during danger or illness
questions.explanation: Emergency contacts connect a learner to trusted help when quick action is needed.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the importance of emergency contacts and help seeking.

questions.prompt: Which practice helps prevent the spread of germs?
options: Cover coughs and wash hands with soap.
Share unwashed cups with many people.
Wipe hands on another learner's shirt.
Leave used tissue on a desk.
questions.correctAnswer: Cover coughs and wash hands with soap.
questions.explanation: Covering coughs and washing hands reduce the spread of germs.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify hygiene habits that reduce disease spread.

questions.prompt: Which is the safest way for a learner to handle medicine at home?
options: Use medicine only with guidance from a trusted adult or health worker.
Take any tablets found in the house.
Share medicine with a friend who has similar symptoms.
Mix different medicines to make them work faster.
questions.correctAnswer: Use medicine only with guidance from a trusted adult or health worker.
questions.explanation: Medicine can be harmful if used incorrectly, so learners need trusted guidance.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safety rules for medicine use and storage.

questions.prompt: A learner faints during assembly. Which response best protects safety while help is coming?
options: Call for adult help, keep the area clear, and avoid crowding.
Give the learner food immediately while unconscious.
Shake the learner hard to wake them.
Take photos before telling anyone.
questions.correctAnswer: Call for adult help, keep the area clear, and avoid crowding.
questions.explanation: In a serious incident, learners should seek adult help and keep the area safe.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze safe learner actions during a school health emergency.

questions.prompt: What does digital citizenship mean?
options: Using technology safely, respectfully, and responsibly
Using the internet without any rules
Sharing private information with strangers
Believing everything seen online
questions.correctAnswer: Using technology safely, respectfully, and responsibly
questions.explanation: Digital citizenship guides safe and respectful behavior in online spaces.
questions.learningOutcome: Define digital citizenship for responsible technology use.

questions.prompt: Which password habit is safest?
options: Use a mix of letters, numbers, and symbols and keep it private.
Use your name only and share it with friends.
Write the password on the classroom wall.
Use the word password for every account.
questions.correctAnswer: Use a mix of letters, numbers, and symbols and keep it private.
questions.explanation: Strong private passwords help protect accounts from misuse.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain habits that protect personal information online.

questions.prompt: Why should a learner think carefully before posting a photo online?
options: Online posts can be copied and shared widely.
Photos posted online always disappear immediately.
Posting photos removes the need for consent.
Every online viewer is a close friend.
questions.correctAnswer: Online posts can be copied and shared widely.
questions.explanation: Digital content can spread beyond the original audience, so privacy and consent matter.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain privacy risks before sharing digital content.

questions.prompt: An unknown person online asks a learner to meet secretly. What should the learner do?
options: Do not meet and tell a trusted adult.
Go alone if the place is nearby.
Send the home address first.
Keep it secret to avoid questions.
questions.correctAnswer: Do not meet and tell a trusted adult.
questions.explanation: Secret meetings with unknown online contacts are unsafe and should be reported.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose safe actions when contacted by unknown people online.

questions.prompt: Which media habit best supports learning and wellbeing?
options: Set a time limit and choose useful content.
Watch videos all night before school.
Believe every forwarded message.
Stop all homework to follow trends.
questions.correctAnswer: Set a time limit and choose useful content.
questions.explanation: Responsible media use includes time control, useful content, and balance with other duties.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply balanced media habits that support learning and wellbeing.

questions.prompt: Which item is a need rather than a want for a learner during the school day?
options: Nutritious lunch
Extra airtime for chatting
A fashion cap
A new video game
questions.correctAnswer: Nutritious lunch
questions.explanation: A need is something important for health, safety, or learning, while a want is optional.
questions.learningOutcome: Distinguish needs from wants in daily learner choices.

questions.prompt: Why can saving small amounts of money be useful?
options: It helps prepare for planned needs and emergencies.
It means a learner should never share or help.
It makes all future problems disappear.
It replaces the need to make a budget.
questions.correctAnswer: It helps prepare for planned needs and emergencies.
questions.explanation: Saving builds discipline and helps meet future needs.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the value of saving and planning for future needs.

questions.prompt: Which action shows care for shared resources?
options: Turn off taps and lights when not in use.
Leave water running after washing hands.
Tear pages from a library book.
Break classroom tools after using them.
questions.correctAnswer: Turn off taps and lights when not in use.
questions.explanation: Taking care of shared resources reduces waste and benefits the community.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify responsible ways of using shared resources.

questions.prompt: Which activity is an example of community service for learners?
options: Cleaning a shared compound with permission and safety guidance
Throwing litter into a drainage channel
Taking tools from a neighbor without asking
Mocking people who volunteer
questions.correctAnswer: Cleaning a shared compound with permission and safety guidance
questions.explanation: Community service is voluntary action that helps others or improves shared spaces.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify age-appropriate community service activities.

questions.prompt: Which class plan best supports environmental responsibility at school?
options: Separate waste, assign rotating cleanup teams, and review progress weekly.
Burn all waste behind the classroom without supervision.
Clean only when visitors are expected.
Move litter from one classroom to another.
questions.correctAnswer: Separate waste, assign rotating cleanup teams, and review progress weekly.
questions.explanation: A good environmental plan includes clear actions, shared responsibility, and review.
questions.learningOutcome: Create practical class plans for environmental care and shared responsibility.

questions.prompt: What does integrity mean?
options: Doing the right thing even when no one is watching
Changing values whenever it is convenient
Hiding mistakes by blaming others
Winning by any method
questions.correctAnswer: Doing the right thing even when no one is watching
questions.explanation: Integrity means being honest and responsible in both public and private actions.
questions.learningOutcome: Define integrity and recognize its importance in daily life.

questions.prompt: A group receives extra marks because of a teacher's recording error. What should the group do?
options: Tell the teacher politely about the error.
Celebrate quietly and hide the error.
Change other groups' marks too.
Blame one member if the error is found.
questions.correctAnswer: Tell the teacher politely about the error.
questions.explanation: Honesty means correcting unfair advantage even when silence would benefit you.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply integrity in situations involving fairness and honesty.

questions.prompt: Which behavior shows good leadership in a class project?
options: Helping others participate and following agreed rules
Taking all materials and refusing to share
Ignoring quiet group members
Changing the plan secretly for personal credit
questions.correctAnswer: Helping others participate and following agreed rules
questions.explanation: Good leadership supports participation, responsibility, and fairness.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain leadership behaviors that support teamwork and fairness.

questions.prompt: Why is a sincere apology important after causing harm?
options: It accepts responsibility and begins repairing the relationship.
It automatically removes every consequence.
It proves the other person was wrong.
It should be used only to avoid punishment.
questions.correctAnswer: It accepts responsibility and begins repairing the relationship.
questions.explanation: A sincere apology recognizes harm and supports restoration when followed by changed behavior.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the purpose of sincere apologies in restoring relationships.

questions.prompt: A learner is not selected for the school team. Which response shows resilience?
options: Ask for feedback and continue practising.
Insult the selected learners.
Quit every school activity forever.
Hide the team's equipment.
questions.correctAnswer: Ask for feedback and continue practising.
questions.explanation: Resilience helps a learner respond to disappointment with learning and effort.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply resilience after disappointment in school activities.

questions.prompt: Which class plan would best help reduce bullying over a term?
options: Agree on reporting steps, peer support actions, and regular class check-ins.
Tell targeted learners to solve everything alone.
Ignore name-calling unless it happens during exams.
Allow learners to punish each other without guidance.
questions.correctAnswer: Agree on reporting steps, peer support actions, and regular class check-ins.
questions.explanation: A strong prevention plan combines reporting, support, shared expectations, and review.
questions.learningOutcome: Create class strategies that prevent bullying and support safe reporting.

questions.prompt: A friend is overwhelmed by a family problem and is missing assignments. Which support plan is most appropriate?
options: Listen privately, encourage trusted adult support, and help plan school tasks.
Tell the whole class so everyone knows the details.
Do all the friend's assignments secretly.
Avoid the friend until the problem disappears.
questions.correctAnswer: Listen privately, encourage trusted adult support, and help plan school tasks.
questions.explanation: Good support protects privacy, encourages trusted help, and addresses practical needs.
questions.learningOutcome: Create supportive responses for peers facing personal difficulties.

questions.prompt: A learner must choose between joining friends who plan to break a rule and attending a planned study group. Which reasoning is strongest?
options: Choose the option that protects safety, values, and learning goals.
Choose the option that avoids all thinking.
Choose the option that makes the loudest friend happy.
Choose the option that can be hidden most easily.
questions.correctAnswer: Choose the option that protects safety, values, and learning goals.
questions.explanation: Responsible decisions consider safety, values, goals, and consequences together.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate options using values, safety, goals, and consequences.

questions.prompt: A learner is repeatedly late to school. Which improvement plan is most complete?
options: Identify causes, prepare items at night, leave earlier, and track arrival times.
Promise to be early without changing any routine.
Blame traffic every day and take no action.
Skip morning duties to arrive faster.
questions.correctAnswer: Identify causes, prepare items at night, leave earlier, and track arrival times.
questions.explanation: A complete plan addresses causes, changes behavior, and checks whether progress is happening.
questions.learningOutcome: Create practical plans for improving punctuality and responsibility.

questions.prompt: Which personal growth plan is most complete for a Grade 7 learner?
options: Set a goal, list steps, choose support, set a timeline, and review progress.
Write a goal once and never look at it again.
Copy a friend's goal without considering personal needs.
Wait for improvement without planning or practice.
questions.correctAnswer: Set a goal, list steps, choose support, set a timeline, and review progress.
questions.explanation: A complete growth plan includes action, support, time, and reflection.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a complete personal growth plan using goals, support, timelines, and review.
